end.summary:
Trisha practised recognising that families can differ in size and members.
They gave examples of care, including medicine, water, sitting together, and visiting a doctor.
They identified that different families can share caring for one another.
The difference between family size and members still needs checking next time; the teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised with Trisha how families may have different sizes and members, while people in families can care for one another. Trisha gave several examples of shared care, such as bringing medicine, giving water, and staying with someone; the family-size idea was partly right but not steady yet. At home, look at two storybook families and ask Trisha to name one difference and one way each family cares for someone.
